podcast.title: Critic Robert Hull's Disparaging Remarks (1975)
podcast.body: In a misogynistic assessment from 1975, critic Robert Hull dismissed Ann Murray as "Ugly" in a crude ranking of female singers he would like "to sit in your lap." "Ann Murray, Ugly"

podcast.title: Duet Performance with Chris Christopherson (1981)
podcast.body: While initially released as a solo record, Ann Murray did perform "Could I Have This Dance" as a duet with Chris Christopherson on her 1981 TV Christmas Special. This fulfilled, in part, her original vision for the song as a duet. "She did sing it with Chris Christopherson on her TV Christmas Special in 1981."

podcast.title: Premature Album Inclusion
podcast.body: So confident in the song's potential, Murray included "Could I Have This Dance" on her greatest hits album even before it was officially released as a single. This decision proved to be prescient given the song's eventual success. "She was feeling so optimistic about this song that she included it on her greatest hits record before it was ever released as a single."

podcast.title: Touring with Jerry Seinfeld
podcast.body: As a young comedian, Jerry Seinfeld worked on the road with Ann Murray, alongside Andy Williams. "He's been working on the road with Ann Murray and Andy Williams."

xref.title: Early Career and Influences
xref.body: He was a young comedian who worked frequently at The Improv Los Angeles and toured on the road with Ann Murray and Andy Williams. He gained notoriety after appearing on The Tonight Show with Johnny Carson, where his act was built on observations about "the madness of life's idiosyncrasies." "Here is a young comedian who works frequently at the improvisation Los Angeles, and he's been working on the road with Ann Murray and Andy Williams."

xref.body: Singer Paul Murray is noted as the nephew of the renowned singer Ann Murray, establishing a familial link to another prominent figure in Canadian music.
